Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority,

IS; 5269 -1987 



Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

ACCESS HATCHES FOR INLAND VESSELS 

( First Revision ) 



( Reaffirmed 2003 ) 



1. Scope — Specifies the dimensions and requirements of hatch coamings and non-watertight 
hatch covers for inland vessels. 

2. Types 

2.1 The hatchway covers shall be of following two types: 

a) Round hatchway covers; and 

b) Square hatchway covers. 

3. Dimensions 

3.1 The dimensions of hatchway covers shall be as given in Fig. 1 and 2.

3,3 The tolerance on all dimensions shall be according to coarse series of IS : 2102-1969 
'Allowable deviations for dimensions without specified tolerances ( first revision )\ 

4. Material 

4.1 The material for the hatchway cover and coaming shall be structural steel conforming to 
15:3039-1980 'Structural steels for construction of hulls of ships {first revision)' or its 
equivalent. 

5. General Requirements 

5.1 When beams are cut in way of the hatches the free edges of the beam shall be rounded off to 
avoid any sharp edges. When more than one beam is cut in way of hatch opening compensation 
shall be provided. 

5.2 A tally piate shall be fixed to each cover as shown in Fig. 1 and 2, on which the designation 
of the cover shall be indelibly marked. 

5.3 Where space permits, at least 150 mm shall be allowed between the hatch coamings and 
adjacent bulkheads, whore applicable, to facilitate maintenance of deck and bulkhead lower 
plating. 

6. Workmanship and Finish 

6.1 The workmanship on the hatchway covers shall be of highest order comforming to the latest 
techniques. All sharp edges shall be rounded off.

6.2 Welding shall be in accordance with IS : 3525-1983 'Code of practice for use of metal arc 
welding for hull construction of nierchant ships in mild steel ( first revision )'. 

7. Weather Protection 

7.1 Where otherwise not specified, two basic primer coatings of paint shall be applied after 
adequate cleaning of the surfaces. 

8. Designation 

8.1 The hatchway covers shall be designated by the type and the number of this standard. 

Example'. 

A round hatchway cover shall be designated as fallows: 
Round hatchway cover IS : 5269. 



IS:526S-1987 

9. Marking 

9.1 The hatch cover shall be marked with manufacturers' name or recognized trade-mark. 

9.2 Standard Mark — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

The location of the access hatchway in inland vessel will depend upon the size of the vessel 
and the type of cargo to be carried. The minimum size of hatchway opening is dictated by the 
requirements for handling a particular commodity. 

By usage, it has been found that the most common size of hatchway opening on inland vessel 
is 600 X 600 mm. This size has been standardized by the European Committee for the Coordi- 
nation of Standards — Inland Shipping Details ( CEN ). In many cases, it has been found round 
hatchway opening of 600 mm is also used. 

Loss of cargo by theft and burglary is a common element of many inland vessels. To offset 
this, it is normal practice in all inland vessels to make suitable arrangement for locking the hatch- 
way cover. 

This standard was first issued in 1969 and the present revision has been taken up to bring the 
standard in line with the current manufacturing practices. Also same vocabulary has been used 
throughout the text of the standard which was not the case in the earlier issue. 



Printed at Printograph, New Delhi, India
